newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares rise a fraction in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares rise a fraction in quiet trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices rose a fraction on Thursday in quiet and largely directionless trading dominated by banks and cements.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index gained 0.05 points to close the day at 357.23 points. Turnover was lower than average at 38.81 million pounds ($11.43 million).
The talk of the market remained the details of the sale of Kabo/Nasr Clothing and Textiles by the state's Holding Company for Spinning and Weaving on Wednesday.

Brokers had spread rumours that the state's National Bank of Egypt stepped in to buy spare shares but the agents for the sale said this was completely untrue. They said they received bids for about two million of the 1.93 million shares on offer.
The new Kabo shares did not trade on Thursday but trading in those Kabo shares privatised earlier closed at 103.00, one pound higher than Wednesday's sale price.
Most active shares on Thursday were Commercial International Bank/CIB and National Societe Generale Bank, but these and other financials showed no clear trend.

"The banks have had a lot of attention recently because the milling sector wasn't doing well and there hasn't been trading in Medinet Nasr Housing and Development," said Mohamed Abdullah of brokers Intercapital.
The partially privatised state mills have been hit by expectations that a new wholly private-sector rival, al-Tahhanoun al-Misriyoun, will cut their profits.
CIB shares closed 1.05 pounds down at 71.95 and National Societe Generale rose 1.66 to 83.50, the CMA said.
Mills were generally higher in unusually low volume, with the exception of Upper Egypt Flour Mills, which fell 0.83 pounds to 78.17, and East Delta Flour Mills, which slipped 0.02 pounds to 65.00.
Cements were busier and mostly weak. Egyptian Tora Portland Cement, the most active in the sector, lost 0.50 pounds to close the trading week at 87.50.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 497.76 from 497.97 points on Wednesday while that for the rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 261.90 points from 261.78.
Out of the 85 shares traded, 41 rose, 24 fell while 20 ended unchanged.
